description: Windows that render untrusted email — thread pop-outs and compose windows (SPEC-P11). Only what they demonstrably call, each scoped to the path it uses, so a sanitizer bypass in one of them costs less. core:path: join() in the attachment cache. core:event listen/unlisten: the IMAP session manager's invalidation listener — no emit, because main acts on events (single-instance-args opens a composer). sql load/select/execute: the database, draft auto-save and the sent copy write (migrations run on mount too; idempotent). opener open-url with the default URL set (http, https, mailto, tel): links in email — not reveal-item-in-dir. dialog save: saving an attachment or an .eml; the picked path is added to the fs scope by the dialog plugin at runtime, which is why write-file and write-text-file need no static path for it. fs, by path: velo.key read-only (credentials decrypt in the page), the attachment cache read/write; deny-default keeps the platform's sensitive paths out. http: the unsubscribe POST and the Ollama provider, with the same scope as main — an accepted residual until both move behind Rust commands. Deliberately absent, each shown main-only by import: webview creation (the pop-out buttons are hidden inside a pop-out), any write to velo.key or the database file, fs:remove, notifications, badge, autostart, global shortcuts, deep-link, updater, process restart, os, and the main title bar's window controls (pop-outs keep native decorations; lib.rs strips them from main only).
